LESSON: ELEMENTS OF AND RESPONDING

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 3.1: Elements of AND RESPONDING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Elements of AND RESPONDING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does it make you a) express initial personal as sad, happy feel?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development
2. use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ELEMENTS OF AND RESPONDING
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Elements of AND RESPONDING helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ELEMENTS OF AND RESPONDING
Study Elements of AND RESPONDING like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development

What this means
In this part you learn to imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Elements of AND RESPONDING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Elements of AND RESPONDING in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Elements of AND RESPONDING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Elements of AND RESPONDING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Elements of AND RESPONDING in your own words. (skill: use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Elements of AND RESPONDING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development.
3. Practise this skill: use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Elements of AND RESPONDING from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Elements of AND RESPONDING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Elements of AND RESPONDING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does it make you a) express initial personal as sad, happy feel?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Elements of AND RESPONDING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: imitate short melodies with asked to imitate them paying accuracy in pitch and rhythm attention to pitch and rhythm for aural development.
5. Be able to: use appropriate terminology in explaining/discussing •.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
